newsitem.title: USA: Investigators split on cause of TWA crash - report.
newsitem.headline: Investigators split on cause of TWA crash - report.

text.p: Some senior National Transportation Safety Board officials now say they believe mechanical failure caused TWA Flight 800 to explode, not a missile or bomb, the New York Times reports in its Sunday edition.
The newspaper said Dr. Bernard Loeb, director of aviation safety for the NTSB, said last week that the missile and bomb theories were now a "lower probability."
He added, "That means there is a higher probability that it's a mechanical issue."

This is the first time since the Paris-bound Boeing 747 exploded on July 17 and crashed off Long Island, killing all 230 aboard, that NTSB investigators have publicly broken with their FBI counterparts to state they think mechanical failure the likeliest scenario, the Times said.
Officials from the safety board have not offered any new evidence to support this view, the newspaper said.
The Times said Loeb's statements were particularly noteworthy because traditionally the NTSB does not comment on any conclusions until evidence is very strong.
Safety board investigators reassembling hundreds of thousands of parts of the plane on Long Island, refused to comment publicly on a theory, the newspaper said.
According to the Times, one senior FBI official said it was "preposterous" to discount the missile or bomb theories while significant gaps remain in reconstructing the wreckage.

Separately, James Kallstrom, head of the FBI in New York told the Times that there was "no evidence of mechanical failure, no evidence of a bomb and no evidence of a rocket, other than some eyewitnesses."

However, the mechanical failure theory still prevails at the safety board in Washington, the newspaper said. "We believe we know exactly what happened," a senior safety board official who spoke anonymously said at its Washington headquarters. "We're missing only a small part of the puzzle."
On Friday, during a media briefing, Kallstrom said the FBI would begin interviewing relatives of the 230 people who died in the crash. The remains of 213 have been recovered.
